chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: Why few jazz musicians write bodies of work
summary: Mingus calls players lazy; Parker wrote blues and new melodies on standard changes.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah. When you think about it, there have been relatively few people in jazz, or whatever you want to call this, who have created a body of work, a real body of written work. There's Duke, of course, and in a small sense, Jelly Roll before him, Monk, in his way, and you can find some

I think because the guys are all lazy, and they want somebody to pave the way for them, they want to play all the standard tunes. They'll take standard chord changes and put melodies to them, at most. That went for Bird, too. I (inaudible) when Charlie Parker didn't write the whole thing. He never wrote a whole composition yet. Take other compositions and put new melodies to them. Or he would write some blues.
He's a master at blues changes.
Yeah. But you're right, he never actually sat down and worked out a wording or something like that.
